transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been feeling completely overwhelmed by persistent, intrusive thoughts that I can't seem to get out of my head. I have this intense, constant fear of contamination and germs, and I'm always doubting whether I've locked my doors or made a mistake. It's getting really hard to manage on my own.
Do you feel compelled to perform specific actions or rituals, such as repeated washing or checking, to relieve the anxiety caused by these thoughts?

Yes, I absolutely feel compelled to do those things. I end up washing my hands constantly because of the fear of germs, and I have to check the door locks and appliances over and over again to ease my doubts. It feels like I have no choice but to do these rituals just to get some temporary relief.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder, Generalized Anxiety Disorder]. The patient's report of persistent, intrusive thoughts regarding contamination and doubt, paired with the clear presence of time-consuming rituals (hand washing, checking locks/appliances) to neutralize the associated anxiety, is pathognomonic for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder and makes Generalized Anxiety Disorder significantly less likely.
